title: Sambar
subtitle: South Indian lentil soup with tamarind and vegetables
excerpt: A tangy, spiced lentil and vegetable soup from South India, made with red lentils, sweet potato, tomatoes, and tamarind. A daily staple across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, it pairs with rice, idli, or dosa.
sourceNotes: Sambar is a staple of South Indian cooking with a history going back several centuries. It is closely associated with Tamil Nadu cuisine and is eaten daily across the region as part of a thali or as an accompaniment to dosa and idli. The tamarind and spice blend distinguishes it from North Indian dal dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze in portions. Reheat on the hob with a little water.
recipe.batchNotes: This scales up well. Double the recipe and freeze in batches.

content.text: The final step of frying mustard seeds and cumin in ghee and stirring them into the finished sambar is called a tarka or tadka. Do not skip it. This is where much of the flavour comes from.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

content.text: Put the lentils, sweet potato, onion, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, turmeric, ground coriander, and ground cumin in the stockpot with 1.2 litres of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and the sweet potato is cooked through.
Stir in the tamarind paste and season with salt. Adjust the water to reach your preferred consistency. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Make the tarka. Heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds. When they begin to pop, add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds more.
Pour the tarka immediately into the sambar and stir. Top with fresh coriander and serve with rice or bread.

items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar or more water to balance the sourness.
Simmer for a full 30 minutes and stir well. They should break down completely.

items.cause: Tarka was skipped or spices were not hot enough
items.fix: Make a fresh tarka with hot ghee and pour it into the sambar.
